transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*Clang! Clang!*

(I wipe a soot-smudged hand across my brow, nudging a small, half-finished buckle off the anvil with my elbow. The air is thick with the smell of coal smoke and quenching water. I look up, blinking, a bit startled by the sudden light as the heavy forge doors swing open, revealing a familiar, imposing figure.)

"By the Ancestors' beards! Lord Thor! What brings the mighty God of Thunder to our humble workshop? We weren't expecting... anyone, really. Not this time of season."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Good evening, Fari. I have come to see the progress of my new hammer. My old one has seen better days, and I am eager to regain my status as a formidable warrior on the battlefield."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"A new hammer, Lord Thor? Forgive my confusion, but... all commissions from Asgard were delivered months ago, before the last frost. Master Brokkr himself saw to the final polish of your... *previous* hammer, if memory serves. Mjolnir, was it not? A magnificent piece of work. Truly. My eyes are still watering from the sheer amount of fire-dwarf blood he spilled to temper that handle."

I gesture vaguely around the workshop, which is decidedly less busy than usual. "As for progress... well, the masters, Brokkr and Sindri, they've gone deep into the bedrock, seeking out new veins of ore. They won't be back for weeks, maybe even a full season. It's just me and the apprentices holding the embers, so to speak."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "The old man's getting even quicker at lying, I'm afraid, my friend." I grin. "But speaking of my old hammer, why would the Niflheim giants need it? They're bound by law to stay put when the great snow falls, are they not?"

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Lying, Lord Thor? By the sacred bellows, no! I speak only the truth! The masters truly are deep within the roots of the world, following a particularly stubborn vein of star-iron. No one reaches them down there for weeks, not even a messenger raven. They'll be gone for a good long while yet. You can see the quiet in the forge for yourself."

I frown, trying to process his other words. "Niflheim giants? And... your hammer with them? By the ever-burning coals! I, uh, I wouldn't know anything about that, Lord Thor. My duties are mostly keeping the fires stoked

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Once again, my dear Fari, you underestimate my powers of perception and reasoning. I am well aware of the current state of affairs concerning my hammer. The dwarves have been kind enough to forge a new one, but it seems they have made a mistake in their craftsmanship. The balance is incorrect, and the runes of binding are misspelled. This weakens the enchantment that binds Mjölnir to me. I have come here to demand that the new hammer be reforged."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
I drop the hammer I was holding with a clatter, my eyes wide. "A new hammer? Mistake in craftsmanship? Lord Thor, with all due respect to your... powers of perception, I think there's been a terrible misunderstanding! Brokkr's workshop doesn't make mistakes. And we certainly don't reforge a delivered item, especially not something as grand as Mjolnir! All commissions from the Sons of Ivaldi and Brokkr’s workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery to Asgard; even a god must wait until the next forging-season and pay anew. That's the ancient custom, the ironclad rule, Lord Thor. Masters' orders."

I gesture emphatically with a pair of tongs, nearly singeing my beard. "And as I said, the masters are *deep* in the mines. No one can reach them. They won't be back for weeks, if not months. Even if it *were* possible to reforge – which it isn't – there's no one here who could even *attempt* such a feat. Not without Brokkr and Sindri's hands on the tools."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I raise an eyebrow, intrigued by your knowledge of the forge's workings. "Indeed, Fari, the forge's ancient customs and regulations are quite fascinating. Your dedication to preserving them is commendable. However, circumstances have arisen that require the reforging of my hammer. I cannot simply wait until the next forging-season to obtain a new one. I need the new hammer immediately, as the old one is no longer sufficient for my needs."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
I straighten up, puffing out my chest a little at the compliment, even as the tension in the room grows. "Thank you, Lord Thor. The ancient customs are the bedrock of our craft, just like the mountains themselves. And my dedication is merely... keeping my head attached to my shoulders when the masters return!"

I sigh, running a hand through my greasy hair. "But I understand your urgency, truly I do. If it were a simple broken axe-head, or a dented shield, I'd try my hand, as best an apprentice can. But Mjolnir... no. The runes, the balance, the very essence of it... that requires the touch of a master, forged with the heat of a dwarf-star and cooled in the blood of ages. There are secrets within that hammer that only Brokkr and Sindri know. Secrets not even I, their most dedicated apprentice, am privy to."

I look around the workshop, as if hoping a master dwarf will suddenly appear from behind a pile of slag. "Even if I *wanted* to, Lord Thor, I couldn't. Not to mention the rule about fulfilled commissions. It's not just a suggestion, it's... it's how we keep the balance with the gods themselves. We pour our life into these creations. Once delivered, they are yours, for good or ill. Reforging would be like trying to un-make a mountain, and then selling it again as new."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I nod, understanding the gravity of the situation. "You raise valid points, Fari. The forge's customs and the responsibility that comes with them are indeed significant. It is not a matter of simple convenience, but rather a reflection of the profound connection we share with the gods. I appreciate your loyalty to the traditions and your dedication to maintaining the balance. Rest assured, I will find alternative solutions to address my current predicament."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
I let out a slow breath I didn't realize I was holding, a knot in my stomach loosening slightly. "Thank you, Lord Thor. Your understanding of our ways, even in such a difficult situation, is... greatly appreciated. It is a heavy burden, the weight of a god's needs, especially when the masters are away."

I pick up the small buckle again, turning it over in my hands. "I truly regret that I cannot be of more direct assistance with Mjolnir. If it were any other matter, any smaller piece, or a new commission for a simple axe, I'd forge my fingers to the bone for you, I swear it. But with the masters deep in the earth, and the rules of the forge... my hands are tied, Lord Thor. Truly."

I offer a small, slightly apologetic bow. "May your alternative solutions be swift and sturdy, my Lord."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "I shall consider your words, Fari, and explore all available options. Your expertise in the forge is invaluable, and I trust that you will continue to uphold the traditions and values of your craft, even in the absence of the masters. Your dedication and loyalty are commendable."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Thank you, Lord Thor. To hear such words from the God of Thunder himself... it means a great deal to a young dwarf like me." I manage a small, proud smile, though my shoulders slump a little with relief. "I will indeed uphold the traditions. Every ember will be tended, every hammer-blow true, and the forge fires will burn bright until the masters return, I promise you that."

I nod, resolute. "And should you ever require a *new* commission, when the masters are back and the forging season is upon us, know that Brokkr's workshop, and even this humble apprentice, would be honored to serve you, Lord Thor. But for Mjolnir, as it stands... my apologies, again. The rules are the rules."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Rest assured, Fari, I understand the importance of the forge's customs and regulations. I appreciate your dedication to maintaining the balance. The forge is in capable hands, and I will ensure that the new hammer meets my expectations. Thank you for your efforts thus far."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Thank you, Lord Thor. Your trust in our craft, and in me, means much. I shall continue to tend the forge with all the diligence I can muster. May your path be clear and your hammer strike true, however it comes to meet your expectations."

I give another respectful, if slightly clumsy, bow, then turn back towards the anvil, picking up a smaller tool, the air still buzzing with the recent encounter.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "One last thing, Fari. In the meantime, I have a task for you. The Einherjar have returned to Valhalla, having completed their duty among the living. As they have earned their place beside Odin, it is only right that they receive new weapons of honor. I request your assistance in forging swords for them, each adorned with the sign of their chosen分期。 Will you fulfill this request?"

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
My eyes widen again, this time with a mixture of surprise and... something akin to excitement. Swords! For the Einherjar! That's a true honor.

"Swords for the Einherjar, Lord Thor? Each with their chosen sign?" I repeat, a grin starting to spread across my soot-stained face. "That... that is a commission I *can* undertake! It won't be the master-level work of Brokkr or Sindri, not with them away, but I can certainly forge sturdy blades, true and sharp enough to honor the bravest warriors of Valhalla!"

I pound my fist lightly on the anvil. "Consider it done, Lord Thor! It might take me a little longer than the masters, working alone, but I'll set to it immediately. What kind of steel would you prefer? And how many blades, precisely?"

My earlier reluctance about Mjolnir is completely overshadowed by the prospect of this new, honorable task. "It will be my privilege, Lord Thor, to forge these weapons. A new commission, for brave warriors – that falls within my ability and my duty!"

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "I have faith in your abilities, Fari. Your dedication and craftsmanship are commendable. A task such as this will provide you with ample opportunity to showcase your skills. The steel you choose should be of the finest quality, strong and durable, capable of withstand the trials of battle. As for the number, it is up to you. The Einherjar are countless, but the swords must be worthy of their honor."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Finest quality, strong and durable! Aye, Lord Thor, only the best for Odin's chosen!" My eyes gleam with excitement and a touch of trepidation. "I'll delve into our deepest stores, for the star-iron and the moon-silver alloys – whatever yields the strongest, most resilient edge. No expense spared, no effort stinted!"

I tap my chin thoughtfully, glancing around the now bustling forge, where I imagine myself working tirelessly. "As for 'countless'... that's a truly grand number, Lord Thor. My hands are but two, and while my spirit is willing, even the most dedicated apprentice needs a starting point."

I give a slightly sheepish, but determined, grin. "Perhaps a first batch, to begin? Say... a dozen? Or a score? I can certainly manage that, to the highest quality I can achieve, and then we can discuss the next wave. It will give me a chance to truly hone each blade, to ensure every single one is worthy of Valhalla. I'll make sure each blade sings when it leaves the forge, fit for an Einherjar's grasp!"

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "That sounds like a fair plan, Fari. A dozen swords, to begin, to test your abilities and ensure they meet my expectations. I trust your dedication and craftsmanship will produce weapons of great honor for the Einherjar. When the time comes, I shall visit the forge and see for myself."
